title: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)

sections.label: SingHealth attack and online avatars
sections.summary: Experts view the SingHealth cyberattack as by a state actor, and critical avatar comments rose during Singapore-Malaysia disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Experts are of the view that the SingHealth cyberattack was by a state actor as the attack continued even after detection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: During the Singapore-Malaysia disputes last year, there was a noticeable increase in critical comments made by avatars.

sections.label: Tighter legislation against external influence
sections.summary: Tighter legislation is needed to deter external pressures from overtly or covertly influencing domestic politics and sensitive issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To do so, we need tighter legislation to deter external pressures from having an overt or covert influence on our domestic politics and sensitive issues, which should rightly be for Singaporeans to decide.

sections.label: Framework to combat fake news
sections.summary: It asks whether MHA would formalise legal tools into a framework to combat fake news from domestic and foreign propagators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: To that end, would the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) consider formalising such an armoury of legal tools into a legislative and regulatory framework to combat fake news emanating from domestic and foreign propagators?

sections.label: Combating hate speech on social media
sections.summary: It asks what steps will combat hate speech inciting violence, citing a 600% rise in racial supremacy tweets since 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Further, what steps will be taken to combat hate speech which incites violence against race or religion where such incitement is conducted on social media?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: It has been reported that since 2012, there has been a 600% increase in the number of users on Twitter globally that spout racial supremacy tweets.

sections.label: Legal tools against inflammatory online speech
sections.summary: It asks what legal tools MHA will deploy against inflammatory speech, noting online falsehoods stoke communal and religious disharmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: As it is more difficult to trace the origins of such speech, and identity can be easily masked, what legal tools will MHA deploy to deter would-be perpetrators from spouting inflammatory speech?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I sat on the Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods last year, and one issue that came up quite strongly was the use of online falsehoods to stoke communal and religious differences and cause disharmony.

sections.label: Controls to safeguard religious harmony
sections.summary: It asks whether legislation or other controls will be developed to safeguard religious harmony given popular foreign preachers' online reach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Foreign preachers, like Mufti Menk and Dr Zakir Naik, are popular online and their reach extends beyond physical space.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In light of the evolving online space and the importance of protecting social cohesion in Singapore, are there plans to further develop legislation or create other controls to safeguard our religious harmony?

sections.label: Guarding against segregationist ideologies
sections.summary: The passage states a need to guard against narrow-minded and segregationist ideologies, citing overseas examples of religious leaders telling followers not to convey well-wishes on others' religious holidays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: In that regard, we need to guard against the rise of narrow-minded and segregationist ideologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: We have seen examples of segregationist ideologies being propagated overseas, such as religious leaders telling their followers not to convey well-wishes to others on their religious holidays.

sections.label: PR status for children
sections.summary: The passage asks whether these children can be granted PR status at least until they reach the age of 21.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can we not grant these children PR status at the very least, until they reach the age of 21?

sections.label: New MHA Science and Technology Agency
sections.summary: The passage states that in January this year, The Straits Times reported MHA will set up a new Science and Technology Agency responsible for research and procurement in border security and critical infrastructure protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in January this year, it was reported in The Straits Times that MHA will be setting up a new Science and Technology Agency, with responsibility in research and procurement areas of border security and protection of critical infrastructures.

sections.label: Home Team Science and Technology Agency
sections.summary: The passage states HSTA will be established to develop science and technology capabilities for the Home Team's operational needs, and the Budget Book states the Home Team is growing in-house scientists and engineers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, it was announced that the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HSTA) will be established to develop science and technology capabilities to support the Home Team's operational needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Budget Book states that the Home Team is growing a pool of inhouse scientists and engineers to develop capabilities in sensemaking and surveillance, biometrics and profiling, forensics and dealing with chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosives incidents.

sections.label: Timing of HSTA establishment
sections.summary: The passage states the decision to establish the new HSTA by the end of this year cannot come soon enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The decision to establish the new HSTA by the end of this year cannot come soon enough.

sections.label: Details on HSTA aims
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister would share more details about the aims and key focus areas of HSTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Minister share more details about the aims and key focus areas of HSTA?

sections.label: E-commerce scams and police manpower
sections.summary: E-commerce scams rose 36.1% between 2017 and 2018, and the speaker asks how the Ministry will ensure sufficient police manpower and whether police can be freed from non-core duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In addition, there is a trend of increasing e-commerce scams which saw an increase of 36.1% between 2017 and 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As SPF is the primary investigative body for such offences, it will have to consequently expand its investigative resources to deal with an expected increase in workload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is not an easy task, given the current geopolitical situation and assessment of security threat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I am heartened to note that in this Budget, there is an increase in financial support to keep Singapore safe and secure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: How will the Ministry ensure that the Police Force has sufficient manpower to handle this expected additional workload?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Is there scope for the Police to be further freed from non-core duties, such as assisting members of public to update changes in their addresses?

sections.label: Drug abusers arrested in 2018
sections.summary: Drug abusers arrested in 2018 rose 11% from 2017, with 3,438 arrested, about 40% below 30, and 40% new abusers, two-thirds of whom were under 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The total number of drug abusers arrested in 2018 increased by 11% from 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Of the 3,438 drug abusers who were arrested in 2018, about 40% or 1,370 of them were below 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In particular, of the total number of drug abusers arrested in 2018, 40% were new abusers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Of these new abusers, about two-thirds, or about 64%, were under 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The numbers suggest that there is a worrying trend where our youths of today have a more liberal attitude towards the use of drugs and are more likely to engage or partake in them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It has been reported in the media just this week that there are plans by MHA to engage youths on the dangers of drug abuse as well as to legislate stiffer laws against the promotion of drugs to youths.

sections.label: CNB drug abuser figures
sections.summary: CNB shared that drug abusers in Singapore in 2018 increased by 11%, with new abusers making up 40% of all cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, earlier this week, CNB shared that the number of drug abusers in Singapore in 2018 had increased by 11%, with new abusers comprising 40% of all cases.

sections.label: Profile of drug abusers
sections.summary: The Minister said abusers' profile changed with the general population, but the speaker worries rehabilitative improvements may favour addicts from more affluent households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister shared during the Debate that the profile of abusers had changed along with the change in profile of the general population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, in the absence of more information on the background of hardcore addicts in Drug Rehabilitation Centres (DRCs) and long-term (LT) imprisonment, I am concerned that the latest rehabilitative improvements may inevitably be tilted in favour of addicts who come from more affluent households.

sections.label: Inmates' employability and employers
sections.summary: The speaker asks what MHA plans to further enhance inmates' employability and how it will work with employers to strengthen ex-offenders' employment outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: The Singapore Corporation of Rehabilitative Enterprises' (SCORE’s) efforts to enhance inmates’ employability would be futile if employers are not receptive to offering inmates jobs when they are released.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: What are MHA's plans to further enhance inmates' employability as part of the rehabilitation efforts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: In particular, how will MHA be working with employers to strengthen the employment outcomes of our ex-offenders?

sections.label: Housing for released inmates
sections.summary: The speaker was informed that homeless inmates are referred to the Family Resource Centre at Singapore Prison Service and interim housing like halfway houses and shelter homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I recently raised a question in Parliament about inmates who do not have a place to stay after their release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I was informed that those who are homeless would be referred to the Family Resource Centre at the Singapore Prison Service, as well as interim housing options, such as halfway houses and shelter homes.

sections.label: PMD and electric bicycle fires
sections.summary: Fires involving electric bicycles, scooters and other PMDs rose by more than 50% from the previous year and caused 22 injuries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: A worrying trend is the number of fires involving electric bicycles and scooters and other personal mobility devices (PMDs).

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: This is an increase of more than 50%, compared to the previous year, and resulted in 22 injuries.

sections.label: Competent Persons for super high-rise buildings
sections.summary: After a 2014 Marina Bay fire killed two security guards, trained Competent Persons were required for Super High-rise Private Residential Buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: After a tragic fire at Marina Bay in 2014, where two security guards died in the fire, the requirement to appoint trained Competent Persons for Super High-rise Private Residential Buildings was implemented.

sections.label: Evacuation gap in public residential buildings
sections.summary: A 64-year-old resident gave up walking and took a lift to evacuate, highlighting no Competent Persons or trained guards in Super High-rise Public Residential Buildings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: A senior aged 64 said he and his family walked from the 48th to the 45th floor, then gave up and took the lift to evacuate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
sentences.text: There is a gap here for Super High-rise Public Residential Buildings, as there are no Competent Persons and trained security guards to help conduct regular public education of residents and facilitate proper evacuation during a fire.

sections.label: 2018 crime rate and online scams
sections.summary: The overall crime rate rose in 2018, mostly from a 20.6% increase in online or phone scams, with foreign syndicates committing a significant proportion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In 2018, the overall crime rate increased, mostly due to a 20.6% increase in scams conducted online or on the phone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Of the online crimes, a "significant proportion" was committed by foreign syndicates.

sections.label: Drink-driving and red-light running accidents
sections.summary: Drink-driving accidents rose 17% from 2017 to 2018, motorcyclist drink-driving accidents rose 51%, and red-light running violations rose 15%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: Drink-driving accidents increased by 17% from 2017 to 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: In particular, the number of motorcyclists who were drink-driving and got involved in accidents increased by 51%!

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: Red-light running violations increased by 15%, with the number of accidents resulting from red-light running increasing by 2.6%.

sections.label: Drivers feeling roads less safe
sections.summary: An AXA Insurance survey showed nearly one in two Singapore drivers feel roads are less safe than three years ago, despite fewer fatal and total accidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: A recent survey by AXA Insurance showed that nearly one in two Singapore drivers feel that the roads have become less safe than three years ago despite a fall in fatal accidents and a drop in the number of accidents.

sections.label: Technology distracts drivers
sections.summary: Technology has made cars and roads safer but also distracts drivers who text, browse social media, or fiddle with devices while driving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: While technology has helped to make our cars and roads safer, technology has also become a source of distraction for many drivers who text or browse social media on their mobile phones, fiddle with their global positioning system or playlist on their devices while driving.

sections.label: Probationary and young drink-drivers
sections.summary: Over five years, an average of 111 probationary drivers and 17 younger drivers were arrested yearly for drink-driving in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In the past five years, the average number of probationary drivers in Singapore arrested for drink-driving per year is 111.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The corresponding figure for younger drivers is 17 per year.

sections.label: Tiered drink-driving system proposed
sections.summary: The speaker recommends the Ministry consider a tiered drink-driving system accounting for alcohol's effect on probationary and young drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: For these reasons, I recommend that the Ministry consider putting in place a tiered drink-driving system that takes into account the effect of alcohol on probationary and young drivers.

sections.label: New Science and Technology Agency
sections.summary: Singapore ranked first in three reports, and a new Science and Technology Agency will transform the Home Team through technology.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Gallup Global Law and Order Report of 2018, the World Justice Project Rule of Law Index of 2019 and the Global Smart City Performance Index of 2018, all ranked us No 1 on this score.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: A significant step this year will be taken to qualitatively improve our capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We are going to set up a new Science and Technology Agency that will help transform the Home Team through the increased use of technology to support operations, for example, through the use of biometric identifiers at our borders, using our sensors to better detect threats, and robotics to automate and streamline processes.

sections.label: Germany's Network Enforcement Act
sections.summary: Germany's Network Enforcement Act requires platforms to remove manifestly illegal content within 24 hours, with fines up to €50 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In Germany, the Network Enforcement Act requires social media platforms to set up a process and the process must ensure that "manifestly illegal content", such as hate speech, should be removed within 24 hours of receipt of a complaint.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Failure to comply could mean fines of up to €50 million.

sections.label: Long-term inmates' wage background
sections.summary: The Government will bring proposals later this year; before changes, nine in 10 long-term inmates were from the bottom 20th percentile of wage earners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Government will come to this House later this year with its proposals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Member did preface his speech by saying he does not have the statistics with him.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, with that caveat in mind, if we look at those in long-term imprisonment, nine in 10 inmates, before these changes were made, were from the bottom 20th percentile of wage earners nationally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Long-term (LT) inmates are drug abusers who have been picked up for the third time or more.

sections.label: SCORE job matching and coaches
sections.summary: SCORE matches abusers to jobs before release and provides job coaches to help them stay employed and earn steady income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: SCORE provides job matching to emplace them in jobs before they are released and job coaches to help abusers stay in employment, draw a steady income.

sections.label: LT scheme and community support
sections.summary: LT inmates go through the now-mandatory scheme, with Prisons and partners helping abusers and families access community resources, and results monitored.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: LT inmates will be put through the scheme and legislation has now made it mandatory.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Prisons also work closely with community partners and other Government agencies supported by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) to ensure that abusers and their families, when they need financial assistance, can tap on community resources, whether at the point when they get admitted into detention or post-release.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We will monitor closely the results from the changes that have been made.

sections.label: Singaporean identity and segregationist thinking
sections.summary: Common experiences must build a strong Singaporean identity, and segregationist thinking, teachings and practices that reduce cross-race and cross-religion opportunities must be guarded against.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We have to build a strong Singaporean identity through these common experiences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We also have to guard against segregationist thinking, teachings and practices that seek to reduce the opportunities for Singaporeans of different religions and races to come together.

sections.label: Singapore value system and religious harmony law
sections.summary: The community must work harder to maintain the Singapore value system, and the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act is being reviewed with details expected later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, we have to work harder in the community to maintain and strengthen the Singapore value system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We also have to review our legislation to deal with some of the challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We are reviewing our Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act in this context.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We aim to give more details later this year, after we have thought through some of the issues and done some consultations.

sections.label: Trust and dialogue platforms
sections.summary: Religious harmony is built on trust among communities, so the Government will keep providing platforms for dialogue and trust-building.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Religious harmony is built and nurtured on the basis of trust among the communities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, the Government will continue to provide platforms to facilitate dialogue and build this trust.

sections.label: Checkpoint traveller and cargo volumes
sections.summary: In 2018 over 212 million travellers and 10 million consignments, containers and parcels crossed checkpoints, with volumes expected to rise by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2018, we saw more than 212 million travellers and 10 million consignments, containers and parcels cross our checkpoints.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: By 2025, we expect cross-border traveller and cargo volumes to increase by around 40% and 70% respectively.

sections.label: BioScreen-MMBS at checkpoints
sections.summary: ICA will implement the BioScreen-Multi Modal Biometrics System across checkpoints later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: ICA will implement the BioScreen-Multi Modal Biometrics System or BioScreen-MMBS, across our checkpoints later this year.

sections.label: PolCams cut harassment cases
sections.summary: Since 2012, PolCams and enforcement efforts have reduced property damage cases from unlicensed moneylending harassment by over 80%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since 2012, PolCams and our enforcement efforts have driven down property damage cases due to unlicensed moneylending harassment by over 80%.

sections.label: Home Team Science and Technology Agency
sections.summary: The fourth area is building a dedicated Science and Technology Agency for the Home Team to augment and maintain its operational edge.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The fourth area is in building a dedicated Science and Technology Agency for the Home Team to augment and maintain the Home Team’s operational edge.

sections.label: Bill for new agency
sections.summary: Four Members asked about plans for and the role of the new agency; a Bill will be tabled to establish a Home Team Science and Technology Agency as a Statutory Board under MHA.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Christopher de Souza, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Low Thia Khiang asked about our plans for and the role of the new agency.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We intend to table a Bill in Parliament to establish a Home Team Science and Technology Agency as a Statutory Board under MHA.

sections.label: Capability development investment increase
sections.summary: The agency will help direct investments in capability development, which will more than double from $979 million in FY2019 to $1.9 billion in FY2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The agency will help to direct our investments in capability development, which will more than double from $979 million in financial year (FY) 2019, to $1.9 billion in FY2025.

sections.label: Agency establishment and existing expertise
sections.summary: The new agency will not duplicate efforts but will tap existing whole-of-Government centres of expertise, with establishment targeted by the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The new agency will not duplicate efforts but will continue to tap on existing whole-of-Government centres of expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We are looking to establish the agency by the end of the year and will provide more details in due course.

sections.label: Reporting suspected Home Team data misuse
sections.summary: A citizen suspecting misuse of personal data by a Home Team Department should approach the Ministry or GovTech, and offenders will be dealt with under the law.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Where a citizen suspects that his personal data has been misused by any Home Team Department, he should approach my Ministry, or GovTech, and action will be taken to investigate.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Anyone found abusing data for unauthorised uses will be severely dealt with under the law.

sections.label: Scam losses in 2018
sections.summary: More than $158 million was lost to scams in 2018, described as a conservative estimate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: More than $158 million was lost to scams in 2018 and this is just a conservative estimate.

sections.label: Joint police operations against scams
sections.summary: Joint operations with Malaysian and Hong Kong police led to over 40 arrests, seizure of over $1.5 million, 600 frozen accounts, and 26 e-commerce scammer arrests.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Last year, Police conducted joint operations with the Royal Malaysian Police and Hong Kong Police, which led to the arrest of over 40 suspects responsible for over 150 Internet love scams across three jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: To date, we have seized more than $1.5 million and frozen over 600 bank accounts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: In just two months, more than 200 e-commerce scam cases were solved and 26 scammers were arrested.

sections.label: Re-employment of retired uniformed officers
sections.summary: MHA re-employed about 45% of retired uniformed officers over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: In the last five years, MHA re-employed about 45% of our retired uniformed officers.

sections.label: Young and youth drug abusers
sections.summary: Abusers below 30 were close to two-thirds of new abusers arrested last year, and new youth abusers below 20 rose 30% to 305.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Young abusers below 30 formed close to two-thirds of new abusers arrested last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: The number of new youth abusers below 20 increased by 30% last year to 305.

sections.label: Drug enforcement and Misuse of Drugs Act
sections.summary: Enforcement continues alongside preventive drug education, and the Misuse of Drugs Act was amended to introduce contamination and child endangerment offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Even as we do more in preventive drug education, we cannot let up on enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: We amended the Misuse of Drugs Act recently to introduce contamination and child endangerment offences.

sections.label: Pure drug offenders rehabilitation
sections.summary: Pure drug offenders will undergo intensive rehabilitation in DRCs instead of long-term imprisonment, with up to five years community supervision after release.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Pure drug offenders will undergo intensive rehabilitation in the DRCs, instead of going through the long-term imprisonment pathway.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: After their release, they will be subject to longer supervision in the community of up to five years.

sections.label: 2018 Malay/Muslim outreach events
sections.summary: Over 50 events were held with 300 organisations, businesses and volunteers, reaching more than 100,000 Malay/Muslims in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Over 50 events were conducted, with 300 organisations and businesses as campaign partners as well as 300 volunteers, and we also reached out to more than 100,000 Malay/Muslims in 2018.

sections.label: Development and Reintegration Programme progress
sections.summary: The Development and Reintegration Programme launched in November 2018 has 185 offenders and families receiving financial assistance, skills upgrading and education for children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: The Development and Reintegration Programme (DRP) that I launched in November 2018 is progressing well.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: To date, 185 offenders and families receive support and help in the form of financial assistance, skills upgrading and education for children.

sections.label: Ex-offenders job placement rate
sections.summary: In 2018, 96% of ex-offenders who requested assistance from SCORE secured a job before release.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: In 2018, 96% of ex-offenders who requested assistance from SCORE secured a job before release.

sections.label: Inmates Higher WSQ certification
sections.summary: Eighty-six inmates attained the Higher WSQ certification as of December 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Eighty-six inmates have successfully attained the Higher WSQ certification as of December 2018.

sections.label: Road Traffic Act penalty amendments
sections.summary: MHA will amend the Road Traffic Act to enhance criminal penalties for irresponsible driving and raise composition sums, and Traffic Police will introduce mandatory simulator training for learner drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To address this, MHA will be amending the Road Traffic Act to enhance criminal penalties for irresponsible driving, especially in egregious cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To complement this, MHA will also raise composition sums for road traffic offences, including the offence of using a mobile phone while driving.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin also asked if MHA will review course requirements for new or inexperienced drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This year, Traffic Police will be introducing mandatory simulator training for all learner drivers, on top of existing course requirements.

sections.label: Deemed drink-driving without exceeding limit
sections.summary: A person is deemed to have been drink-driving if he consumed alcohol and could not control his vehicle, even without exceeding the statutory alcohol limit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: A person would also be deemed to have been drink-driving as long as he has consumed alcohol and had been unable to control his vehicle, even if he did not exceed the prescribed statutory alcohol limit.

sections.label: Fire safety measures in building design
sections.summary: Such buildings are required to incorporate fire safety measures in their design, such as refuge floors and fire lifts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: First, we require such buildings to incorporate various fire safety measures in their design, such as refuge floors and fire lifts.

sections.label: Amending Fire Safety Act for older buildings
sections.summary: MHA will amend the Fire Safety Act to require owners of selected older buildings to carry out critical fire safety upgrades, prioritising high-risk industrial buildings, public buildings and hospitals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To ensure that older buildings are also upgraded with time, MHA will be amending the Fire Safety Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Owners of selected older buildings will be required to put in place critical fire safety upgrades.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will prioritise high-risk industrial buildings, public buildings and hospitals, and work closely with their owners to ensure that the new requirements are practicable.

sections.label: Radicalised Singaporeans dealt with under ISA
sections.summary: Since 2015, 24 radicalised Singaporeans have been detected and dealt with under the Internal Security Act.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since 2015, 24 radicalised Singaporeans have been detected and dealt with under the Internal Security Act.

sections.label: Singaporeans' awareness and readiness on terror
sections.summary: Three in four Singaporeans are aware of SGSecure, one in two believe we are well-prepared for a terror attack, and almost all believe we will stand united.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Today, three in four Singaporeans are aware of SGSecure, one in two Singaporeans believe that we are well-prepared to handle a terror attack on our shores, and almost all Singaporeans believe that we will stand united in the face of an attack.

sections.label: Police handling of appeals and representations
sections.summary: The Police will consider all proper representations, including from elected Members of Parliament and GRAs, assessing all appeals on their own merit, while representations by non-elected Members of Parliament are treated as personal appeals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Police will consider all proper representations which include representations from elected Members of Parliament and from GRAs on behalf of their own constituents, and their grassroots leaders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: All appeals will be assessed on their own merit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Representations by non-elected Members of Parliament, such as NCMPs and Nominated Members of Parliament (NMPs), will be treated as personal appeals by the appellants.

sections.label: Why legal adoption is needed
sections.summary: Legal adoption is needed because without it there is no biological or legal nexus between a Singaporean stepparent and his foreign stepchild.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, perhaps let me explain why legal adoption is needed in the first place.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Without legal adoption, there is no biological or legal nexus between a Singaporean stepparent and his foreign stepchild.

sections.label: Adoption of foreign stepchildren
sections.summary: MSF allows a shorter process for adopting foreign stepchildren, and the Family Justice Courts appoint a guardian to conduct social investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For the adoption of foreign stepchildren which Mr Png asked about, MSF already allows for a shorter process and the Family Justice Courts will also appoint a guardian in adoption to conduct social investigation, to assess the prospective adopters' parenting capacity and the family's circumstances.

sections.label: Not making knowledge an offence
sections.summary: Policy considerations for not making it an offence are hard to answer broadly and depend on various factors, but such a person would be well advised to report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If it is not an offence, what are the policy considerations for not making it an offence?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It will be difficult and unwise to give a broad answer to a question like this.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Is it just pure knowledge, is it something more?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think it depends on a variety of factors, but such a person who knows of a potential terrorist action would be well advised to report to the agencies.

sections.label: Agencies respond to MP appeals
sections.summary: When the person writing the appeal holds an appointment as a Member of Parliament or a GRA, the agencies will respond and deal with it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We want to try to help the residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, in order to help the resident, when the person who is writing the appeal comes within the rules, as in, he holds an appointment either as a Member of Parliament or as a GRA, the agencies will respond, will deal with it and will respond.

sections.label: Weight given to proper appeals
sections.summary: Other representation is treated as an individual representation, while appeals by Members of Parliament and GRAs are assessed in accordance with the rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Any other representation from anyone else will be treated as an individual representation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Now, in terms of the status, the weight that is to be given to appeals, proper appeals, appeals by Members of Parliament and GRAs, the fact will be considered and they will be assessed in accordance with our rules.

sections.label: Agencies assess grey-area discretion
sections.summary: The Police will look at whether it is an appropriate case for discretion to be exercised, and everything is put in writing to check conformity with the rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Trying to persuade the agencies, that this is the case that comes in a grey area where some discretion ought to be exercised.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And the agencies which deal with it, the Police, will have to look at it, see whether it is an appropriate case for discretion to be exercised, and deal with it, and it is all put in writing, so that everything can be looked at, and see whether it conforms to our rules.

sections.label: Withdrawal of amendment
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Chairman for leave to withdraw his amendment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: With that, Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
